dish: Kushikatsu skewers (lotus root, asparagus, beef) and doteyaki (beef sinew stewed in miso)
address: Jan Jan Yokochō (Nan'yō-dōri), Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka
w: Counter-only kushikatsu shop under the red-nosed tengu mask in Jan Jan Yokochō; Inside Osaka names it among Shinsekai's best for consistently queue-worthy skewers, and Shobunsha's co-trip singles out its miso doteyaki.

dish: Tsurigane manjū (bell-shaped castella bun filled with koshian)
w: Founded 1900 (Meiji 33) when a great bronze bell was donated to Shitennō-ji; the bell-shaped bean-paste manjū it began selling at the temple gate is still the Tennōji meibutsu, per All About and Go Live Travel Japan.

dish: Mixed juice (ミックスジュース) and cold coffee
address: Jan Jan Yokochō, Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka
w: Started as a fruit shop in Jan Jan Yokochō in 1948 and claims to be the birthplace of Osaka's mixed juice — ripe fruit blended at the counter — becoming a kissaten in 1955; covered by Rurubu, Waraku and Daily Sports.
